headline: At 76, Australian Doctor Plants Legacy Across 120 Hectares
meta_description: A retired general practitioner in Western Australia has restored 120 hectares of native vegetation, turning a conservation dream into a multigenerational legac…
summary_short: Susan Downes bought a farmhouse expecting quiet countryside life. Nearly two decades later, the 76-year-old has restored thousands of native trees across her property.
body: Susan Downes bought an old farmhouse in York, Western Australia, imagining a quiet life with a small garden. Instead, she inherited stewardship of a 200-hectare property—and nearly two decades of purposeful restoration work. The retired general practitioner discovered a hill where ancient native trees had survived over a century of grazing, yet the vegetation beneath them had vanished. What began as an unexpected challenge became her life's most meaningful project. At 76, Downes has now restored 120 hectares of the property, replanting thousands of native trees and returning the land to ecological health. Her work transforms what could have remained a depleted landscape into a thriving forest—one that will sustain wildlife and community wellbeing for generations to come. The story reminds us that conservation is never too late to begin, and that one person's dedication can reshape an entire ecosystem.
quick_facts: Retired Australian GP Susan Downes, 76 years old
Restored 120 of 200 hectares in York, Western Australia
Nearly two decades of native tree planting and vegetation recovery
Hill with century-old native trees required ecological restoration beneath canopy
